title: Fix the Unsynchronized Shared Counter
description: The program should have two threads each increment a shared counter 100,000 times, ending at 200,000.
expectedBehavior: After both threads finish, count should reliably equal 200000.
actualProblem: count++ is not atomic — it involves a read, an increment, and a write. When two threads perform this on the shared count at nearly the same time without synchronization, some increments can be lost, so the final total is usually less than 200000 and varies between runs.
explanation: Concurrent, unsynchronized modification of shared mutable state is a race condition — the outcome depends on unpredictable thread timing. Wrapping the increment in a synchronized method ensures only one thread updates count at a time, making the result deterministic.
